new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word accent on the penultimate syllable; individual exceptions marked with an acute in the vocabulary.

new_statements.identity_note: 'Marudu Dusun' = Dusun of the Marudu Bay district; the largest Dusunic group there is Kimaragang (kima1244), with Tobilung, Sonsogon, Garo/Talantang and Tinagas villages also in the district. Rutter does not name the village or subgroup, so the column cannot be equated with Kota Marudu Talantang; recorded here only as a district-level pointer (group-level statement) [name in source: Marudu Dusun (one of the 13 vocabulary columns); pages pp. 262 (note), 263-275 (vocabulary)]

sources.citation: Goliu, Percy (ed. desk 'Editor'). 2023-08-21. 'Percampuran suku Liwan dan Bundu pengaruh dialek Dusun Talantang' [The mixing of the Liwan and Bundu tribes influences the Dusun Talantang dialect]. TALANTANG.com (Malay-language community news site, Kota Kinabalu), reporting independent researcher Isahak Sanudin's 2019 Kadazandusun regional seminar paper on the Dusun Talantang dialect. Companion item 2023-07-19 'Sejarah Dusun Talantang kurang dikenali, perlu dikaji' not downloaded (the Internet Archive's index lookup returned 'Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline'; not re-queued under the window rule).
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent, tone or intonation (no occurrence of tekanan / nada / intonasi / aksen). The dialect content is segmental and lexical only: (i) presence vs absence of 'H' distinguishes Liwan from Talantang -- 'Menurut Isahak, huruf H adalah yang membezakan dialek Dusun Talantang dan Liwan' with pairs konihab/koniab 'yesterday', hilo/silo 'there', kinorohingan/kinoringan 'God', tohun/toun, koruhang/koruang 'friend'; (ii) Liwan diphthongs and vowel sequences ai au ua ou oi are not pronounced as such in Talantang and are replaced by near-equivalents, e.g. Liwan waig 'water' vs Talanta…

sources.note: Describes Tandek Kimaragang [kqr], not Talantang; mentions a 'Kimaragang-Garo' sub-dialect (Kg. Longob, Masolog) which Kroeger 1985 identifies as Kimaragang of mixed Kimaragang/Garo descent, i.e. not the Talantang/Garo language. Its stress section (sec. 4) is not in the scan. Not usable for grm.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul R. 1985. Linguistic relations among the Dusunic groups in the Kota Marudu District. Borneo Research Bulletin 17(1): 31-46.
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 'Tinagas / Garo' and 'Kota Marudu Talantang' (p.21) give ethnonyms, settlement history (Kg. Talantang founded by Talantang from the Sugut River) and lexicostatistics (83% cognate with Sugut Talantang, 85% with Parong, 80-81% with Tandek Kimaragang); only phonological remark in the article is Pitas vs Tandek Kimaragang voiced stops. The word 'stress' does not occur in the article.

sources.citation: King, Julie K. & John Wayne King (eds.) 1984. Languages of Sabah: a survey report. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. [Smith, 'The languages of Sabah: a tentative lexicostatistical classification' 1-49 (sec. 2.3.9.4.10 'Garo' = Talantang KM); King, 'The Rungus language' 283-296 (sec. 3.1.2); Banker & Banker, 'The Kadazan/Dusun language' 297-324 (sec. 3.4 'Garo language', Figs. 21-22)]
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistics and intelligibility testing at Talantang KM ('The people from Talantang KM use the autonym Garo'); Banker & Banker sec. 3.4 establishes Garo as a language distinct from Kimaragang (<80% intelligibility). No phonology; 'stress'/'accent'/'penult' occur nowhere in the volume.
